documents.unit: University of Colorado system (Office of Policy and Efficiency), applies to CU Boulder
documents.title: APS 6012 - Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: A University of Colorado system policy on responsible AI use effective August 2026. It sets rules on data protection, intellectual property, procurement, disclosure and conduct, creates campus and system AI committees, and leaves coursework decisions to schools and faculty.
documents.stance_why: The policy states "this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework" and lets "Schools, colleges, departments, or academic programs" set guidance, so it sets no coursework stance itself and hands the decision down.

units.why: The brief description states the university is "committed to supporting the responsible exploration" of AI and "encouraging and supporting innovation". It is an institution-level statement of purpose and principles, so P56 fits; it is not a rule for coursework.
units.anchor: committed to supporting the responsible exploration of the rapidly growing field of AI tools
units.frag_end: in alignment with its mission and values.

units.why: The "Reason for Policy" says the policy "establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI". This states purpose and scope at institution level (P56).
units.anchor: establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI

units.why: The definition "Generative AI (GenAI) is a subset of Artificial Intelligence" fixes what the policy covers, so it is a definition (P61, informs).
units.anchor: Generative AI (GenAI) is a subset of Artificial Intelligence (AI) that can generate text,

units.why: The policy quotes Regent Law and says "This principal responsibility includes decisions about the use of AI tools", placing pedagogy-related AI decisions with faculty. That is who decides (P04), not an AI stance.
units.anchor: This principal responsibility includes decisions about the use of AI tools within those contexts
units.policy: Faculty have principal responsibility for decisions about the use of AI tools in pedagogy, curriculum, research and scholarly work, consistent with other Regent Laws and Policies.
units.fit_note: Decision rests with tenured and tenure-track faculty collectively through governance, not necessarily the individual instructor.

units.why: "final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President and the Chancellors" names who holds authority outside Regent Law 5 contexts, which is P80 (who owns the policy).
units.anchor: final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President

units.why: "must comply with CU's data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies" binds any AI use for University activities to existing policies (P77, must).
units.anchor: must comply with CU’s data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies
units.frag_start: The use of any AI tool
units.policy: Use of any AI tool, stand-alone or embedded, for University academic, research, scholarly and creative work or administrative activities must comply with CU's data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies.

units.why: "Users need to consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide to GenAI tools" tells users to protect what they enter, which is P50.
units.anchor: Users need to consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide

units.why: The same sentence adds users must evaluate "the quality and accuracy of the output", a verify-the-output rule (P31); the privacy half of the sentence is coded separately as P50.
units.anchor: evaluating the quality and accuracy of the output of the system
units.policy: Users evaluate the quality and accuracy of the output of the GenAI system.

units.why: "AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements" is a general conduct ban on deceptive use, and the passage extends to "the integrity of ... teaching, or other academic work" (P74).
units.anchor: AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements or controls

units.why: "individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI" lets people and units opt out of AI for particular activities and set alternatives. Closest is P04 (local decision), and it is about opting out rather than a per-instructor rule.
units.anchor: individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI
units.policy: Individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI and may establish appropriate alternative processes where feasible.
units.fit_note: Covers units and individuals deciding certain activities go without AI and setting alternative processes, not specifically instructors choosing a course rule.

units.why: "maintain and prioritize human judgment and creativity" states that AI use must not displace human thinking. P32 (people remain the thinker) is the nearest type, though the passage is addressed to all users, not students.
units.anchor: maintain and prioritize human judgment and creativity
units.fit_note: Addressed to all users and to research and service as well as learning; not specific to students.

units.why: "Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system" keeps humans accountable for decisions. P73 is nearest, but the sentence is general, not limited to decisions about individuals.
units.anchor: Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system
units.fit_note: General rule that accountability for any decision or outcome stays with humans; P73 covers decisions about individuals specifically.

units.why: "Users must recognize that AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information and should exercise judgment" warns that output can be wrong or biased and asks for critical judgment (P31).
units.anchor: AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information

units.why: "should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services" directs people to human support in sensitive personal matters (P72); it concerns wellbeing, not coursework.
units.anchor: should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services
units.fit_note: About emotional and psychological matters, not academic help.

units.why: The policy says AI procurement and use decisions "should, where feasible, consider resource consumption and environmental impact". It names an environmental cost concern (P53).
units.anchor: consider resource consumption and environmental impact as part of broader technology evaluation

units.why: "This Policy governs the use of AI for University activities by all CU students, faculty, staff" sets who and what the policy covers (P61, scope).
units.anchor: This Policy governs the use of AI for University activities by all CU students,

units.why: "All use of AI for University activities must comply with applicable laws, regulations, and University policies" ties AI use to existing law and policy (P77, must).
units.anchor: All use of AI for University activities must comply with applicable laws,

units.why: "Users of AI tools must adhere to campus IT acceptable use policies" binds AI use to an existing policy (P77).
units.anchor: Users of AI tools must adhere to campus IT acceptable use policies

units.why: "may only be entered into AI approved for the applicable data classification" limits confidential data to approved tools, a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: may only be entered into AI approved for the applicable data classification

units.why: "input of confidential and/or highly confidential data into an AI tool that has not been reviewed and approved ... is strictly prohibited" is an outright ban on one kind of input (P50).
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited
units.policy: Entering confidential or highly confidential data into an AI tool that has not been reviewed and approved for use by campus IT is strictly prohibited.

units.why: "AI tools may not be used in ways that violate conduct expectations for CU faculty, staff and students" ties AI use to the code of conduct (P77).
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used in ways that violate conduct expectations

units.why: "may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses without their express permission" protects faculty course materials from AI tools. P49 (do not upload course materials) is nearest; here the protected party is the faculty member and the concern is training.
units.anchor: may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses
units.fit_note: Concerns faculty IP and use for model training or secondary uses, with an exception by faculty permission; P49 is about students uploading materials.

units.why: "Students retain ownership of their original work" states who owns student work, which is about ownership of AI inputs and outputs and IP (P52).
units.anchor: Students retain ownership of their original work
units.frag_end: applicable law or contractual obligations provide otherwise.

units.why: "Users are responsible for ensuring that such records are retained, managed, and disposed of" applies records law to prompts and outputs. No type is about records retention, so P77 (comply with existing law) is the nearest.
units.anchor: AI-related content, including prompts, outputs, and related records that are retained
units.fit_note: Specifically requires prompts and outputs to be managed under records retention rules.

units.why: "The procurement of AI tools must follow the University's procurement policies and procedures, including appropriate fiscal, cybersecurity and accessibility reviews" requires review before buying AI (P65).
units.anchor: The procurement of AI tools must follow the University’s procurement policies and procedures

units.why: "Users may not input, upload, or provide data to any AI tools if doing so would violate legal, contractual, or licensing restrictions" bans inputs that break legal or contractual limits (P50).
units.anchor: Users may not input, upload, or provide data to any AI tools if doing so

units.why: "Prompts, outputs, and related records ... may be subject to disclosure upon request" under the Colorado Open Records Act tells users their AI prompts are not private. P50 (protect data, tools store prompts) is the nearest.
units.anchor: Prompts, outputs, and related records (including logs, where applicable) may be subject to disclosure
units.frag_start: As a public institution, the University
units.frag_end: exempt from disclosure under applicable law.
units.fit_note: Public-records disclosure of prompts and outputs rather than vendor storage.

units.why: "AI-derived content used for official communications must comply with branding, communication, marketing" rules, an operational rule for official content (P76).
units.anchor: AI-derived content used for official communications must comply with branding

units.why: "University data ... must not be used for external or commercial AI model training unless explicitly authorized" limits sharing university data with AI providers (P65).
units.anchor: must not be used for external or commercial AI model training unless explicitly authorized

units.why: "The University will maintain and communicate guidance on approved AI tools" commits the university to publish an approved-tool list (P92, use approved tools).
units.anchor: The University will maintain and communicate guidance on approved AI tools

units.why: "The University shall establish a structure of advisory committees to inform and support decision making regarding the procurement and use of AI tools" names who oversees the policy (P80).
units.anchor: shall establish a structure of advisory committees to inform and support decision making
units.frag_end: scope of responsibility to ensure that their actions are well informed.

units.why: "Each campus Chancellor ... shall appoint a Campus AI committee(s) to implement this Policy on their campus and develop further campus-specific policy" assigns implementation and local rules to a body (P80).
units.anchor: shall appoint a Campus AI committee(s) to implement this Policy on their campus
units.frag_start: Campus AI Committees: Each campus Chancellor

units.why: "campus faculty shared governance bodies are responsible for establishing and maintaining faculty-led committees" gives faculty bodies ownership of academic AI guidance (P80).
units.anchor: campus faculty shared governance bodies are responsible for establishing and maintaining faculty-led committees
units.frag_start: Faculty AI Committees: Consistent with shared

units.why: "individual faculty shall ensure that AI use aligns with academic standards, disciplinary norms, institutional practices, and pedagogical goals" makes faculty responsible for fitting AI to pedagogical goals (P83).
units.anchor: individual faculty shall ensure that AI use aligns with academic standards, disciplinary norms
units.fit_note: Also names academic standards, disciplinary norms and institutional practices, not only learning objectives.

units.why: "The President shall appoint a Systemwide AI Committee to support coordination and oversight of AI use across the University" creates the system-level oversight body (P80).
units.anchor: The President shall appoint a Systemwide AI Committee to support coordination and oversight
units.frag_start: Systemwide AI Committee: The President shall

units.why: "Before implementing or deploying any new AI tool ... all University units must ensure that appropriate review and approval processes are followed" requires review before deploying a tool (P65).
units.anchor: Before implementing or deploying any new AI tool for University Activities

units.why: The review list includes "Accessibility requirements under applicable laws and University policy", so accessibility is part of tool review (P97).
units.anchor: Accessibility requirements under applicable laws and University policy
units.fit_note: One item in a list of review criteria for AI tools.

units.why: "Users must disclose their use of GenAI to an appropriate audience when such use contributes to University decisions or other high-impact outputs" is a disclosure duty, limited to official capacity and high-impact outputs (P24).
units.anchor: Users must disclose their use of GenAI to an appropriate audience
units.frag_start: Disclosure of GenAI Involvement: Users must
units.policy: Users must disclose their use of GenAI to an appropriate audience when such use contributes to University decisions or other high-impact outputs created in an official University capacity.
units.fit_note: Applies to official University capacity and high-impact outputs, not to coursework.

units.why: "individuals using GenAI are responsible for reviewing outputs for accuracy, appropriateness" is a duty to check output because GenAI can fabricate (P31).
units.anchor: individuals using GenAI are responsible for reviewing outputs for accuracy, appropriateness

units.why: "this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework" says the policy sets no coursework rule, so decisions go to instructors and units (P04).
units.anchor: this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework
units.frag_end: use of AI tools in coursework.
units.fit_note: The decision is handed to schools, colleges, departments and programs rather than to instructors alone.

units.why: "Schools, colleges, departments, or academic programs ... may establish guidance regarding the use of GenAI in coursework" lets academic units set their own rules (P85).
units.anchor: may establish guidance regarding the use of GenAI in coursework or instructional activities
units.frag_start: Schools, colleges, departments, or academic programs,

units.why: "Faculty shared governance bodies and professional academic organizations can develop best practices" for GenAI in research is a rule about who sets research AI practices (P62).
units.anchor: Faculty shared governance bodies and professional academic organizations can develop best practices

units.why: "University staff may use GenAI tools to support administrative, operational, and service functions" allows staff operational use under conditions (P76).
units.anchor: University staff may use GenAI tools to support administrative, operational, and service functions

units.why: "Supervisors and units may establish additional guidance for the appropriate use of GenAI in administrative functions" lets units add local administrative rules (P76).
units.anchor: Supervisors and units may establish additional guidance for the appropriate use of GenAI

units.why: "must not be created or distributed without their explicit, informed consent" bans AI likenesses of real people without consent (P74).
units.anchor: must not be created or distributed without their explicit, informed consent
units.fit_note: Includes an exception for academic freedom and extends to public-facing university content.

units.why: "GenAI tools may not be used to intentionally create sexualized content ... depicting real individuals" is a conduct ban on harmful content (P74).
units.anchor: GenAI tools may not be used to intentionally create sexualized content

units.why: "Users of GenAI tools must perform due diligence to ensure that outputs do not infringe copyright" is a duty about copyright of AI output (P52).
units.anchor: must perform due diligence to ensure that outputs do not infringe copyright

units.why: "Policy violations may result in disciplinary action ... student conduct processes" says violations go through existing discipline. P36 is nearest although it does not classify AI use as misconduct in particular.
units.anchor: Policy violations may result in disciplinary action consistent with applicable University policies
units.fit_note: Names employee discipline, student conduct, loss of access and legal remedies; general rather than academic-integrity specific.

units.why: "This Policy will be reviewed on a periodic basis and more frequently as needed" commits to revisiting the policy (P54).
units.anchor: This Policy will be reviewed on a periodic basis and more frequently as needed

units.why: The definition "AI tool – a commercial or non-commercial technology that includes artificial intelligence-based capabilities" sets scope to include embedded AI and community-built tools (P61).
units.anchor: a commercial or non-commercial technology that includes artificial intelligence-based capabilities

units.why: "supporting ... appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities" is an equity aim in the ethical principles. P51 is nearest though it is a principle, not a no-paid-tools rule.
units.anchor: support appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities
units.fit_note: A principle of equitable access, with no statement about cost or alternatives.

documents.unit: Boulder Faculty Assembly and Center for Teaching & Learning
documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Syllabus Guidance
documents.summary: A draft from the Boulder Faculty Assembly and Center for Teaching and Learning that gives instructors recommended syllabus language and four use categories to pick from. It also advises against AI detectors and suggests discussing or co-designing the policy with students.
documents.stance_why: The guidance offers four templates, "Full", "No", "Conditional" and "Limited" Gen AI Use, and asks "Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit", so it hands the choice to instructors and lists tiers.

units.why: "living document that will be amended in response to significant developments" says the guidance is provisional and will change (P54).
units.anchor: living document that will be amended in response to significant developments

units.why: "Let these four levels of use kick off the conversation" offers named levels (Full, No, Conditional, Limited) as the way to sort AI use (P05).
units.anchor: Let these four levels of use kick off the conversation

units.why: "educators should communicate to students their policies regarding the use of these tools in coursework" asks instructors to state expectations to students (P09, should).
units.anchor: educators should communicate to students their policies regarding the use of these tools
units.fit_note: Recommended, not required, and not tied to the syllabus alone.

units.why: "ethical, privacy, security, environmental, financial, and accessibility concerns" are listed as considerations when forming a policy. P53 is nearest; the list also covers cost and accessibility.
units.anchor: ethical, privacy, security, environmental, financial, and accessibility concerns
units.fit_note: Lists several concerns (privacy, cost, accessibility) beyond ethics and environment.

units.why: "Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit gen AI usage" leaves the choice to the instructor and asks only for a clear statement (P04).
units.anchor: Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit gen AI usage

units.why: "A thoughtful conversation with students addressing your expectations about gen AI use can encourage open dialogue and promote trust" gives a reason to talk the rules through with students (P66).
units.anchor: A thoughtful conversation with students addressing your expectations about gen AI use

units.why: "Consider co-designing a gen AI use policy with your students collaboratively" suggests setting the policy together with students (P67).
units.anchor: Consider co-designing a gen AI use policy with your students collaboratively

units.why: Detectors "are unreliable and not recommended, as they can generate false positives and be biased against students for whom English is a second language" is an anti-detector rule (P39).
units.anchor: are unreliable and not recommended, as they can generate false positives

units.why: "If you plan to use any gen AI detection, you should disclose this in your syllabus and in dialogue with your students" has instructors disclose their own use of detection to students (P47).
units.anchor: If you plan to use any gen AI detection, you should disclose this in
units.fit_note: Disclosure concerns detector use on student work.

units.why: "consider whether students can meaningfully consent to use of such tools to assess their work" raises student consent to detector use. No type covers consent to being checked, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: consider whether students can meaningfully consent to use of such tools
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should weigh whether students can meaningfully consent to AI detection tools being used to assess their work.

units.why: The note says the statements "were developed using the Pepperdine Generative AI Syllabus statement Tool and adapted for use at CU Boulder" and describes how the guidance was made (P84).
units.anchor: developed using the Pepperdine Generative AI Syllabus statement Tool
units.frag_end: adapted for use at CU Boulder.

units.why: The template defines AI as "software that reproduces text, images, computer code, audio, video, and other content", setting what the statement covers (P61).
units.anchor: software that reproduces text, images, computer code, audio, video, and other content

units.why: "This statement governs all such tools, including those released during our semester together" extends the template to future tools (P61, scope).
units.anchor: This statement governs all such tools, including those released during our semester

units.why: "relying on a gen AI tool may result in your submission of inaccurate content" warns students the tools are not built for accuracy (P31).
units.anchor: relying on a gen AI tool may result in your submission of inaccurate content

units.why: "It is your responsibility—not the tool's—to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work you submit" makes students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: It is your responsibility—not the tool’s—to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work

units.why: "If gen AI tool use is suspected ... I will follow up with you" commits the instructor to talk to the student first (P57).
units.anchor: If gen AI tool use is suspected in completing assignments

units.why: "I may contact the Office of Student Conduct & Conflict Resolution to report suspected Honor Code violations" treats unauthorized AI use as an Honor Code matter handled by the conduct office (P36).
units.anchor: I may contact the Office of Student Conduct & Conflict Resolution

units.why: "you must be wary of unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication" warns students that AI use can cause plagiarism or fabrication by accident. No type fits that warning, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: you must be wary of unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication
units.uncovered_note: Students must watch out for unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication when using AI.

units.why: "it is recommended that you incorporate one of the following four categories" has instructors choose one named category for their classroom (P05).
units.anchor: it is recommended that you incorporate one of the following four categories

units.why: "use these categories to specify allowable use for individual assignments" lets instructors set the rule assignment by assignment (P04).
units.anchor: using these categories to specify allowable use for individual assignments

units.why: The Full Gen AI Use template says "You may use gen AI tools in this course however you see fit", an open permission (P02).
units.anchor: You may use gen AI tools in this course however you see fit

units.why: "some assignments will require the use of such tools" builds AI into assigned work (P79).
units.anchor: some assignments will require the use of such tools

units.why: "keep in mind your own and others' privacy implications and security risks when using gen AI tools" tells students to protect privacy (P50).
units.anchor: keep in mind your own and others' privacy implications and security risks

units.why: "document your usage with the Chicago Manual of Style or appropriate citation guidelines" requires students to cite AI use; it recurs in each permitted tier and is coded once (P24).
units.anchor: document your usage with the Chicago Manual of Style or appropriate citation guidelines
units.frag_start: If you use gen AI tools

units.why: "consider providing alternative methods that do not require gen AI use" asks instructors to offer non-AI routes for access, cost and privacy reasons (P51).
units.anchor: consider providing alternative methods that do not require gen AI use

units.why: The No Gen AI Use template says "You may not use gen AI tools on any assignments in this course", a full ban (P01).
units.anchor: You may not use gen AI tools on any assignments in this course

units.why: "consider including clarifying language as to why and to outline consequences of gen AI use" asks instructors who prohibit AI to give reasons and consequences (P66).
units.anchor: consider including clarifying language as to why and to outline consequences

units.why: The sample wording says AI "will not enhance student learning, nor serve the topic at hand", a reason for the ban. P41 is nearest although the claim is that AI does not help learning, not that it shortcuts practice.
units.anchor: will not enhance student learning, nor serve the topic at hand
units.fit_note: Says AI does not enhance learning or serve the topic, not that it replaces practice.

units.why: The sample says if use is suspected "I will consult with you and ask that you redo the assignment using no gen AI", an educative remedy (P68).
units.anchor: ask that you redo the assignment using no gen AI

units.why: "clarify whether use of tools such as Grammarly and Spellcheckers is acceptable or unacceptable" asks instructors to rule on grammar tools separately (P18).
units.anchor: clarify whether use of tools such as Grammarly and Spellcheckers is acceptable or unacceptable

units.why: The Conditional template says "You may conditionally use gen AI tools in this course on any assignment" with conditions the instructor inserts, a named tier (P05).
units.anchor: You may conditionally use gen AI tools in this course on any assignment
units.fit_note: Conditions are left for the instructor to fill in.

units.why: "with clear attribution and explanation of AI's role in the completion of the assignment" is a disclosure condition that goes beyond a citation (P24).
units.anchor: with clear attribution and explanation of AI's role in the completion of the assignment
units.fit_note: Asks for an explanation of AI's role as well as attribution.

units.why: The Limited template says AI may be used "on specific assignments in this course, but their use is limited to the following particular tasks", a narrow-use tier (P05).
units.anchor: their use is limited to the following particular tasks
units.frag_start: You may use gen AI tools on specific

units.why: The example "generating ideas or outlines, but the final work must be student-generated" allows brainstorming only, with student authorship of the final work (P15).
units.anchor: generating ideas or outlines, but the final work must be student-generated

units.why: The example "grammar checks but not for rewriting sections of the assignment" allows grammar help but not rewriting (P91).
units.anchor: grammar checks but not for rewriting sections of the assignment

units.why: "you may have some assignments for which you require gen AI use for specific pedagogical purposes" tells instructors they may require AI in some assignments (P79).
units.anchor: you may have some assignments for which you require gen AI use

units.why: "clearly describe how gen AI use meets the learning goals of the assignment" asks instructors to tie required AI use to learning goals (P83).
units.anchor: clearly describe how gen AI use meets the learning goals of the assignment

units.why: "take into consideration accessibility parameters" asks instructors to account for accessibility when requiring AI (P97).
units.anchor: take into consideration accessibility parameters

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Security Guidelines
documents.summary: A campus IT security page with guidelines for using generative AI tools safely. It limits AI tools to public data unless reviewed, tells users to verify output and review AI-written code, and points to the NIST AI risk framework.
documents.stance_why: The page is about data security and says "AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public" and to "Use AI tools available and recommended", so it permits AI use under data conditions and sets no coursework rule.

units.why: "Implementation of AI is subject to all applicable CU Boulder policies, standards and guidelines" ties AI to existing campus policy (P77).
units.anchor: Implementation of AI is subject to all applicable

units.why: "This page is intended to guide our community as you consider using AI on the CU Boulder campus" states the purpose of the page (P56).
units.anchor: This page is intended to guide our community as you consider using AI

units.why: "As the uses and ramifications of AI ... continue to evolve" signals that the guidance will change over time (P54).
units.anchor: As the uses and ramifications of AI as a technology tool continue to evolve

units.why: "Use AI tools available and recommended for use on the CU Boulder campus" tells people to use campus-recommended tools (P92).
units.anchor: Use AI tools available and recommended for use on the CU Boulder campus

units.why: "AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public" limits what data can go into AI tools (P50).
units.anchor: AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public

units.why: "the service needs to be reviewed for compliance with CU's data security requirements via ICT Review" requires review before confidential data goes to an AI service (P65).
units.anchor: the service needs to be reviewed for compliance with CU’s data security requirements via

units.why: "Information shared with Generative AI tools using default settings is not private" warns that prompts may be exposed (P50).
units.anchor: Information shared with Generative AI tools using default settings is not private

units.why: "Review AI tool output to verify integrity: the output should be accurate and not incomplete, incorrect, or biased" requires users to check output (P31).
units.anchor: Review AI tool output to verify integrity

units.why: "AI-generated computer code should NOT be used for institutional IT systems and services unless it has been reviewed by a human" allows AI code only after human review. P16 is nearest; here the rule is for institutional systems, not coursework.
units.anchor: AI-generated computer code should NOT be used for institutional IT systems and services unless
units.frag_end: accuracy, security (ensuring no vulnerabilities are introduced), and efficiency.
units.fit_note: Applies to institutional IT systems and services, and the condition is human review for accuracy, security and efficiency.

units.why: "must read and understand the AI tool vendor's policies" asks all users to learn vendor terms and data handling (P52, terms of use). Nearest type; the passage is also about data storage.
units.anchor: must read and understand the AI tool vendor’s policies
units.frag_start: Faculty, staff, and students using these
units.fit_note: Also asks users to understand how the vendor stores and handles CU data.

units.why: "you will need to consider the potential positive and/or negative impacts it will have on the campus, your department, and your personal life" asks users to weigh impacts before using AI. No type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: you will need to consider the potential positive and/or negative impacts
units.uncovered_note: Users must consider the positive and negative impacts of AI on campus, department and personal life.

units.why: "A great framework to help you determine whether an AI tool is reliable and/or truthful is the NIST AI Risk Management framework" recommends a framework for users to judge tools. No type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: A great framework to help you determine whether an AI tool is reliable
units.uncovered_note: Recommends the NIST AI Risk Management framework as the way for users to evaluate whether an AI tool is trustworthy.

units.why: "standards and expectations for bias minimization should be defined prior to using AI" asks for bias standards before use (P53).
units.anchor: standards and expectations for bias minimization should be defined prior to using AI
units.fit_note: Framed as a trustworthiness attribute of AI systems.

units.why: "understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information" says people should know when they deal with AI content (P103).
units.anchor: understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information
units.fit_note: A definition of transparency in the NIST framework, not a duty.

notes: Course layer deferred and no school or computing-unit policy found per collect file. The OIT page gives no coursework stance, so permit was chosen for its data-conditioned allowance; delegates is a defensible alternative. The CTL guidance is a draft dated 2024-12-23. Several units were coded UNCOVERED (consent to detectors, unintentional plagiarism warning, impact consideration, NIST framework).
